Hi Emma — good questions. High-level proposal attached (clearline_commit_matrix_v1.xlsx) and summarized below. I copied Jordan (tech lead — capacity) and Diego (onboarding PM) so we can nail dates and validation criteria.

Summary proposal (first pass)
- Commit: 60 steady reserved GPU-hours / day (equivalent to X vGPU units) for 12 months, with a staged ramp to 100% over 2 weeks after canary success.
- Target hardware: mixed A100-40GB primary with fallback to A100-80GB and a dedicated small A10 pool for lower-cost async batches.
- Validation cadence: three-phase (staging smoke, canary traffic, peak soak):
  1) Staging smoke (2 days): functional checks, model correctness with 200–500 sample requests.
  2) Canary (72 hours): 5% production mirrored traffic to dedicated fleet. Success = <5% error rate, 95th pct latency within SLA target (200ms generation).
  3) Peak soak (24 hours): ramp to 70% of expected peak (i.e., ~140 qps). Observe cost/unit and memory pressure.
- Cutover windows: target weekend (Fri 22:00–Mon 04:00 PT) with a 2-hour blackout at the start for KV cache warm-up and prefix priming.
- Rollback triggers: sustained >10% error increase or 95th pct latency >350ms for >10 minutes during canary/soak.

Action items for Clearline engineering:
- Confirm token/session distribution and any heavy long-context endpoints (we saw one long-tail endpoint in the sample).
- Approve the proposed 72-hour canary window and a weekend cutover range.
- Provide legal PO/commit sign-off target date to align DocuSign.

If that looks good, Jordan will follow up with an exact GPU baseline and Diego will propose a final cutover calendar.

Thanks,

Soojin Lee
Strategic Sales Manager | Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwoodinference.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 15:30:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Clearline sizing assumptions + recommended cutover checkpoints

Quick internal note — assumptions we should validate with Emma: token averages, peak concurrency, percent of streaming responses. My recommended sizing map and sequence:

1) Baseline fleet: 6x A100-40 (reserved) + 2x A10 (burst/async). Map the Relevance model to 4 A100-40, LLM-chat variants to the other 2; reserve a 10% headroom for autoscale burst.
2) Batching: configure dynamic batching with max_batch_tokens=2048 and target latency ceiling at 200ms for 95th pct. Use a conservative batch timeout (6ms) in canary.
3) KV cache warm-up: pre-warm top 50 prefixes (customer-provided) during blackout start; we should script priming via 2 concurrent workers to avoid cache stampede.
4) Canary staging: begin with 3% mirrored traffic for first 12 hours, escalate to 5% for remaining 60 hours if stable. Canary route must be able to fallback to hosted instance automatically on error.
5) Roll-forward plan: if canary meets success criteria, schedule full traffic ramp in 25/50/75/100% steps across 6 hours (observe at each step for 20 mins).

I'll prepare a short playbook (ops checklist + runbooks) and share before the proposed cutover weekend.

- Jordan

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Proposed cutover window + acceptance gates (Clearline)

Emma — following our internal alignment, attached is the formal cutover timetable (cutover_timetable_v3.pdf) and a short acceptance checklist. Key points below:

Cutover weekend: Sat Sep 19 22:00 PT — Mon Sep 21 04:00 PT (primary window).
Pre-cutover (Fri 12:00–22:00 PT): final smoke in staging and runbook rehearsal with Clearline engineers (shared Zoom).
Blackout start (Sat 22:00 PT): 2-hour KV cache warm-up + prefix priming. No production schema changes during blackout.
Canary (Sun 00:00–Sun 03:00 PT): 3% mirrored traffic for 12 hours then 5% for remainder; success criteria repeated below.
Soak & Ramp (Sun 12:00–Sun 20:00 PT): 25/50/75/100% steps per Jordan's sequence with 20-min observation windows.
Rollback windows: automatic fallback to hosted API route if error >10% or 95th pct latency >350ms sustained for 10+ minutes.

Acceptance gates (must be green before ramp to 50%):
- <5% relative error rate vs hosted baseline
- 95th pct latency <= 200ms (generation only)
- No OOMs or memory pressure >80% on reserved instances

DocuSign for the committed capacity addendum will be sent once you confirm the weekend and acceptance gates. DocuSign link: https://docusign.com/transaction/ABC123example

Can you confirm by EOD next Tue (Sep 7) so legal can sign and we can lock the reserved pool?

Thanks — we'll own the orchestration and the automatic fallback; Diego will schedule the rehearsal slot.

Best,

Soojin
